cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Can You Keep It?
cards.instruction: Use increasingly sensitive details to test whether someone deserves deeper trust.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's handle this professionally. I withdrew my college application. Have you told Mum?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She asked. I said my sister's plans were hers to explain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can explain the standard again. Slowly. Then there's more. I've leased a bakery. Can I send you the address?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Call me. Mum uses my tablet; she'd see the message.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good catch. I'll call. It's Mum's old bakery. I want you there when I tell her.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 gives deeper news and A5 adds Mum's bakery connection, so D131 is clear. The professional lecture is not a correction of B2's good discretion.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 protects A's choice, leading to A3 lease disclosure; B4 shared tablet risk causes A5 phone choice. The standard-again phrase does not fit that competence.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 both protect A usefully, giving a genuinely cooperative sibling interaction.

heightening.evidence: A5 rewards B4 privacy judgment with the most sensitive family connection and a support request.
